chunks: Al-Husayn, from Safwan, from al-Ala', from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from one of the Imams (peace be upon them (peace be upon them both), said:
I asked him about a group of people in a village: do they pray Friday prayer in congregation? He said, 'Yes, and they pray four [rak'ahs] if there is no one to deliver the khutbah (sermon).'
ai.seo_question: How many rak'ahs are prayed for Friday prayer if there is no one to deliver the sermon?
ai.summary: This narration from the chain of Imam al-Husayn clarifies the flexibility of Friday prayer in smaller communities, establishing that the absence of a formal preacher (khatib) does not invalidate the obligation but rather modifies its form. In Shia jurisprudence, this supports the view that the khutbah is a recommended condition rather than a strict pillar for validity, allowing the prayer to proceed with four rak'ahs when a speaker is unavailable. This ruling highlights the practical adaptability of Islamic worship in varying social structures.
